test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The marked price of an article is kept at 25% above the cost price. If the article is sold at a discount of 8%, find the ratio of its selling price to its cost price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 125 − 8% of 125 = 125 − 10 = 115.

Ratio of **SP : CP** = 115 : 100 = 23 : 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 23 : 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/675e2b6d3861a15adb57ada3865382498f3fb3e12925487b480bffa0214b53c4.png] 

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 25%

Discount Percentage = 8%

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **CP** = 100 units

⇒ **MP** = 100 × (125/100) = 125 units

⇒ **SP** = 125 × (92/100)

⇒ **SP** = 125 × (23/25) = 5 × 23 = 115 units

⇒ Ratio **SP : CP** = 115 : 100

⇒ Dividing both by 5, Ratio = 23 : 20

**∴ The correct answer is 23 : 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Profit Percentage

The net profit percentage can be calculated using the formula: %Profit = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%)/100.

Relation between CP and MP

CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This is useful when profit percentage is given instead of selling price ratio.

Successive Percentage Change

Marking up and then discounting is a form of successive percentage change: Final Factor = (1 + m/100) × (1 − d/100).</p
